correctness.rationale: Positivity and equality at the Rayleigh quotient of 1 imply that 1 is an eigenfunction, since the positive operator ||T||I-T has vanishing quadratic form there. The discarded disks contribute exactly r_j^2 c_j^n to each analytic moment; the centered outer disk contributes zero for n>=1. The first q nonconstant moments for q distinct nonzero centers give an invertible shifted Vandermonde system, contradicting their positive weights unless there are no nonzero centers. Disjointness then permits at most one positive-radius hole. For the concentric annulus, the ratio of its nth eigenvalue to b-a is S_n=sum_{j=0}^n b^{n-j}a^j, with S_{n+1}<= (a+b)S_n, strictly for n>=1 since a>0. The n=1 mode gives necessity of a+b<=1 and the recurrence gives sufficiency, including exactly two top modes at equality. Without holes the disk eigenvalues are b^{n+1}. The normalized constant/linear block has diagonal m and b^2-a^2-2a|c|^2 and off-diagonal modulus sqrt(2)a|c|. Its larger eigenvalue gives the strict bound. Along signed real displacement t, the disk moment integrand extends using factors (u+t)^j and (conj(u)+t)^k. In a complex t-neighborhood with r+|t| bounded by a fixed rho<1, the resulting matrix series converges absolutely in trace norm (geometric decay times sqrt((j+1)(k+1))). This justifies isolated analytic perturbation with compact positive real operators. In the simple case the constant diagonal is fixed and the only first-order coupler is -sqrt(2)a to e1 with gap m(1-a-b), yielding the stated second-order coefficient; unitary rotation by pi makes the branch even, so the next possible term is fourth order. At equality the derivative on the double eigenspace has slopes +sqrt(2)a and -sqrt(2)a, and the max gives exactly the stated cusp. Rotation handles complex displacements. These are exact operator arguments, not extrapolations from a finite compression.

value.rationale: Circular perforations form a natural multiply connected test class for the reverse area problem in wavelet/Bergman concentration. The exact threshold distinguishes when a fixed radial aperture really minimizes norm at its area, and the strict eccentric lower bound plus both sharp local coefficients show how much performance changes under alignment errors on either side of a simple-to-double top eigenvalue transition (the subcritical range and its endpoint). The counterexample identifies the limitation of the broad radial-equality remark.
residual_risks: No monotonicity over the full eccentric range or classification of noncircular holes follows. The expansion on the supercritical side is not claimed.
